title: Niccolò Guidi di Bagno to the Secretariat of State, Paris, 5 January 1652 (AAV Francia 104; DECODE R5622)

documents.shelfmark: AAV Segreteria di Stato, Francia 104, ff. 5r-7v; DECODE R5622
documents.route: Paris -> Rome (Niccolò Guidi di Bagno -> Secretariat of State)

plaintext.source: No decipherment, clear copy or edition found.

transcription.notes: Four cipher pages; OCR and glyph segmentation were too inaccurate for publication.

system.summary: Unseparated decimal stream with Italian words left clear; code boundaries and values are unknown.
system.notes: Repeated 66 and 666 exclude the Francia 346 convention in which 6 is a separator and never part of a code.

prior_solution.where: No edition or decipherment found; DECODE has no transcription or attached document.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: supplied an authenticated DECODE session and posed the target with the suggestion to test the Francia 346 key. No target-specific reading or transcription was supplied.

solution.what: Downloaded and inspected all five authenticated DECODE images.
Checked the exact shelfmark and adjacent DECODE records; no same-text or same-key sibling was found.
Tested Lasry's reconstructed Francia 346 key; its mandatory 6 separator is incompatible with R5622's repeated 66 and 666, and a checked line gives malformed groups and no Italian.
Tried whole-line OCR, digit segmentation and glyph clustering on ff. 6r-7v.
Searched exact shelfmark, sender, date and route and checked the Ranuzzi/Acta Nuntiaturae Gallicae lead; no edition of this despatch or online decifrati register was found.

outcome.method_basis: No key, decipherment or clear copy was found; Lasry's Francia 346 key was ruled out structurally (its separator 6 conflicts with repeated 66/666), and OCR transcription was too noisy to use.
outcome.notes: Attempted, open. Francia 346 is excluded; needs a reliable manual transcription and the 1652 Paris nunciature key or Secretariat decipherment.

gaps.detail: no matching key, decipherment or clear copy; Francia 346 excluded
human-readable scans, but OCR and automatic segmentation are not reliable enough
